title: 1957 AHSME Problem 38
statement: From a two-digit number \(N\) we subtract the number with the digits reversed and find that the result is a positive perfect cube. Then:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: \(N\) can end in any digit other than \(5\)

solutions.text:
Writing \(N=10a+b,\) the positive difference is \[ \begin{aligned} &(10a+b)-(10b+a)\\ &\quad=9(a-b). \end{aligned} \] It is at most \(81.\) Among \(1,\) \(8,\) \(27,\) and \(64,\) only \(27\) is divisible by \(9,\) so \(a-b=3.\) The digit pairs are \[ \begin{gathered} (3,0),(4,1),(5,2),(6,3),\\ (7,4),(8,5),(9,6), \end{gathered} \] giving exactly seven values of \(N.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: If the digits are \(a>b,\) the difference from the reversal is \(9(a-b)\)
The difference is at most \(81,\) so test the positive cubes no larger than \(81\)
